analysis.evidence: בְּרֵאשִׁית places the creation of the heavens and the earth in time. Whether the verse opens ‘In the beginning God created’ or ‘When God began to create,’ רֵאשִׁית denotes the beginning of creation.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ ‘in, at’ prefixes a feminine singular noun, parsed here as absolute. The noun has the same form in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb בָּרָא. The two direct objects, אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם and וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ, identify what God created.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of בָּרָא, “created.” The verb is third-person masculine singular, identifying God as the single creator of the heavens and the earth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of בָּרָא ‘created’. The marked אֵת introduces הַשָּׁמַיִם ‘the heavens’, the first of the verb’s two coordinated definite objects.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The repeated object marker in אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ pairs the heavens and the earth as the two objects of בָּרָא. Together they express the whole of creation.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: וְאֵת marks הָאָרֶץ as the second direct object of בָּרָא. Paired with הַשָּׁמַיִם ‘the heavens’, it denotes the earth as a whole.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute, in pausal form אָרֶץ.
